The ATTEND study collects clinical records, radiology imaging, IHC, and WES-derived
genomic features (TMB, MSI, HRD, aneuploidy, and a per-variant MAF) on the **same
patients**. These reports link the modalities onto a shared patient ID, assemble a
per-patient master table, and analyse it.

**There is no build order.** The join lives in code/build_master.R, and every report
calls get_master(), which reads the master table when it exists and builds it when it
does not. Any report can be the first one knitted, and wflow_build() with no arguments
is always correct.

Each report opens with a four-line scope contract: the question, the cohort, what it
reads, and what it deliberately leaves to another report. They are numbered in reading
order, 00 to 11.

**[00 — Methods](00-methods.html)** carries every justification in the pipeline, and the
shared definitions each report links to rather than repeating: the two TMB definitions, the
aneuploidy classes, what "MMR-deficient only" means, the highlight groups, and how the
master is built. Operational recipes — running GISTIC on the cluster, classification
alternatives — live in runbooks/.

### Integration and QC

- **[01 — Data integration and quality control](01-data-integration.html)** · all patients
  Part 1 translates three ID spaces onto one patient key, collapses each modality to one
  row per patient, and writes the master. Part 2 audits what that cost: unmapped records,
  coverage per dataset, the UpSet of who has which modality, and value sanity. Part 3 asks
  whether the automated FlowPath quantification agrees with the pathologist's eye — a
  measurement-validation question, so it sits with the other checks on the inputs rather
  than beside the biology it feeds.

### Clinical outcome

- **[02 — Survival](02-survival.html)** · all patients
  Every Kaplan–Meier and Cox model in the pipeline: treatment arm within panels defined by
  aneuploidy × MMR, then TMB, HRD, MSI, and immune content.
- **[03 — Covariate distributions by MMR status](03-covariates-by-mmr.html)** · all patients
  ECDF and Kolmogorov–Smirnov per continuous covariate, plus the aneuploidy score itself
  contrasted between MMR-deficient and -proficient tumours.

### Aneuploidy and the tumour microenvironment

- **[04 — Aneuploidy in MMR-deficient tumours](04-aneuploidy-mmrd.html)** · MMRd only
  Part 1 takes aneuploidy against mutation status, one gene at a time. Part 2 takes it
  against FlowPath cell-type composition under three normalizations.
- **[05 — Treatment response and cell-type composition](05-response.html)** · all patients + MMRd
  The composition panels of report 04 Part 2, re-keyed on treatment response — a 6-month
  landmark on the survival endpoint, with patients censored before the landmark reported as
  unclassifiable rather than counted as failures. Every figure is drawn for the whole cohort
  and for the MMR-deficient stratum, and one interaction model tests whether they differ.

### Mutation burden and molecular class

- **[06 — Tumour mutational burden and the ancestry correction](06-tmb.html)** · all patients
  Part 1 asks whether TMB resolves the hypermutator population as a genuine second mode.
  Part 2 draws TMB by aneuploidy once per MMR stratum. Part 3 replicates the whole battery
  in TCGA UCEC, which is tumour-normal paired. Exactly two definitions are ever reported:
  the upstream tumour-only score, and the same score after the Nassar ancestry recalibration.
- **[07 — Molecular classification: the TCGA cascade and ProMisE](07-molecular-classification.html)** · all patients
  Two classifications on the same patients, drawn side by side. The 2013 TCGA cascade
  (Kandoth et al.) clusters GISTIC thresholded peaks with Euclidean distance and Ward.D2
  linkage, sweeps k = 2–8 on one chromosome heatmap, and calls serous-like directionally.
  Beside it, **ProMisE / WHO-ESGO** — POLEmut > MMRd > p53abn > NSMP, the algorithm WHO 2020,
  ESGO/ESTRO/ESP and FIGO 2023 staging actually specify — with POLE *screened* by
  exonuclease-domain hotspot rather than assumed absent, and every patient it cannot classify
  reported as unclassifiable rather than defaulted into NSMP. Both calls annotate the Fig-1a
  heatmap, so a disagreement reads as a vertical mismatch.
- **[08 — TP53 and the gene panels](08-tp53-and-gene-panels.html)** · all patients
  The genes report 07 uses as single binary markers, looked at properly: oncoplots, the
  configured MMR and Wnt panels, OncodriveCLUST positional clustering, and the TCGA Fig. 2d
  mutation-frequency comparison across the aneuploidy × MMR subgroups.

### Copy number, and the external reference

- **[09 — TCGA UCEC 2013, Fig. 1a on TCGA's own data](09-tcga2013-fig1a.html)** · TCGA UCEC 2013
  Report 07's figure, built the same way, on the cohort where **the right answer is
  published**. Clusters TCGA's own published GISTIC peaks — no parameter guess, no GISTIC run,
  no liftover — and scores the recomputed partition against `CNA_CLUSTER_K4` with an adjusted
  Rand index. Also draws what the 2013 paper could not: aneuploidy against its four SCNA
  clusters, since that score is retrofitted from PanCancer-Atlas.
- **[10 — Recurrent copy number in aneuploidy-high tumours](10-recurrent-cna.html)** · all patients, then MMRd-high vs MMRp-high
  Two questions, in order. **Are there recurrent CNAs in MMRd aneuploidy-high tumours?** —
  per-peak recurrence inside that stratum alone, with Wilson intervals, against a cohort-wide
  baseline. **If so, are they the same ones that recur in MMRp aneuploidy-high tumours?** —
  the mirror plot, the pre-specified TCGA locus panel (confirmatory, Holm), the data-driven
  panel whose selection is nested inside the permutation (exploratory, and permanently so),
  peak-set overlap across the five GISTIC runs, and leave-one-out stability.
- **[11 — MMRd aneuploidy: metastatic vs primary](11-mmrd-crosscohort.html)** · MMRd only, both cohorts
  Does aneuploidy substructure MMR-deficient tumours in **metastatic** disease (ATTEND) in a
  way that is absent from **primary** disease (TCGA UCEC)? Five parts: whether the split is
  present in each cohort, whether MMRd aneuploidy is absolutely higher in metastatic disease,
  how many MMRd tumours are aneuploidy-high in each, whether TMB tracks aneuploidy within an
  MMR stratum, and the TCGA MMRd survival split — including why it cannot decide anything.
  This is the report `attend_cohort_cols` exists for: TCGA is the external reference, so it
  takes the reference grey and only ATTEND carries a hue.

### Conventions

Shared definitions are written **once**, in [00-methods](00-methods.html), and linked from
the reports that use them rather than rendered into each one. Reports show derivations and
results, and carry no takeaway or interpretation sections: conclusions belong in the
manuscript, where they can be revised as the data changes.

Every chunk that produces a figure or table is preceded by a derivation note saying what is
shown, where it comes from in the raw data, and which operations change its interpretation.

code/tests/test_rmd_style.R enforces the structure and code/tests/test_rmd_parse.R
checks every chunk parses. Both are base R, so they run without tidyverse or the cohort.

### Configuration lives in one place

- code/build_master.R — the join, the crosswalk assembly, and get_master().
- code/attend_harmonise.R — ID spaces, the two crosswalks, the collapse-to-patient rule.
- code/attend_classes.R — column names (attend_cols), thresholds, class derivation,
  gene panels, the TMB definitions and labels, and the CNV/TCGA-cascade config.
- code/attend_plots.R — the one palette (Tol vibrant), attend_theme(), attend_box(),
  and the highlight overlay with its crosswalk-aware id resolution.
- code/attend_ihc.R — FlowPath IHC metric definitions (reports 02, 04, 05, 06).
- code/attend_scna.R — GISTIC peak union, panel score, permutation and LOO stability.
- code/attend_bimodality.R — tmb_long(), tmb_battery(), and the bimodality measures.
